description:
LANDED ca23b676f on wt/kdt-close (PR #110, draft), 2026-09-03. Re-cut on
fz-kdt.192 (which deleted the pattern-witness machinery this ticket used to
edit), cold-reviewed APPROVE (the latency concern resolved decisively).

THE CHANGE: a @spec type variable's polarity splits its bounds. arrow_match.rs
BindingSide { Unify, Lower, Upper } with a total flipped(); the single walk
over (params, args) that fz-kdt.192 left records into MatchBounds { lower,
upper } by polarity; collect_arrow_match is the ONE reversing node (an arrow's
parameters flip Lower<->Upper); instantiation reads the LOWERS only (their
join); the meet of the UPPERS is the SOLVABILITY CHECK -- join(lowers) not a
subtype of meet(uppers) is Invalid, a NECESSARY CONDITION over variables both
bounds reached, over observed lowers, before close_bounds (not "iff"). A
variable with ONLY upper bounds stays FREE -> Underconstrained.
collect_instantiation_subst stays the Unify/Unify unifier (its four callers --
semantic.rs ground_instance, types/mod.rs grounded_callable_args and
specialize_callable_clause, sigs.rs specialize_lit_arrow -- are byte-
identical); collect_constraint_subst is the new solver entry.

THE DEFECT (live at base, proven by the pins): before this, an arrow
PARAMETER witness (an upper bound: the callee's function must ACCEPT it) was
unioned into the lower solution as if it were evidence. A4:
f(a, (a)->nil) :: (a)->nil at (int, (any)->nil) instantiated a := any and
answered Known (any)->nil -- UNSOUND, since (int)->nil is a supertype of every
legal instantiation and (any)->nil claims the produced function accepts what
the callee never promised. A5: the same spec `when a: int` answered Invalid, a
FALSE violation on a legal call. Both are reproduced by constructing the Ty
inputs and calling match_arrow -> instantiate_match; the fix takes A4 to
Known (int)->nil and A5 to Known int.

WHY IT MOVES NO CORPUS FIXTURE (the fz-kdt.143 category): the frontend demand-
narrows a callback's parameter to the covariant element type before the
calculator sees it -- a predicate declared (integer | binary) -> :ok handed to
a walker arrives as (int) -> :ok -- so base's polluting union is always
idempotent on the shipped library, and no shipped @spec returns an arrow
carrying a variable in its parameter. The fix forecloses the unsound class on
a shared surface; it is correct by construction, not dead code. This is stated
as a guidepost in the arrow_match module doc so a future reader does not
mistake the 0-mover latency for inertness.

RED-FIRST: 15 pins flip at base (built a base test binary, applied the pin
literals over base production -> 15 failed / 37 passed, each showing base-
actual vs new-expected). Soundness A4/A5/X2/X2B; precision A3/A13/R1/R3/R4/R7/
R9v2/R16 (any -> int under contravariant parameters); documented Known ->
Underconstrained regressions A2/R6/R14 (an only-upper variable stays free),
named in the module doc as the observable consequence. At HEAD pinned_verdicts
is 52/52 green. fix-2 ("never record an upper bound of none") is STRUCK: R20
is Underconstrained at base AND head, so it is unneeded. fix-3 is a one-line
`if !has_vars(witness)` guard.

RIP-OUT: no single-polarity Sigma helper survives the collector walk (all six
thread MatchBounds); the empty-list cleaner keeps NO polarity threading (it
reads the lower side) and is left inert for fz-kdt.120 to delete -- 120's
OpenVars.positive IS this BindingSide, so 120 re-cut on this folds positive ->
BindingSide, adds OpenVars.vars (openness, a distinct axis), and deletes the
cleaner.

MEASURED (597 fixtures, against 343f3a134): interp 0 movers, run 0 movers,
canon md5 0 movers (469 backend programs, identical set). lib 1699/0/5; matrix
506/0/9; fmt/clippy/build/doc clean.

RESIDUES: fz-kdt.120 (deletes the cleaner, folds the polarity); fz-kdt.197
(the non-ground Known -- X2/X2B flip the pure-contravariant-var case here, the
gate half 197 credits to this ticket; 197's own Range.reduce_while_cont rows
are unchanged). Pre-existing: 00424_protocol_no_impl.fz panics at
artifact.rs:155 (fz-kdt.149); --emit=stats session counters are scheduler-
nondeterministic (canon md5 is the faithful comparand).

GATE: Coordinator gate on the folded commit (marker COORD-GATE-1788452303): fmt clean, zero build warnings, clippy clean, doctests clean, lib 1703 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored, fixture matrix single-threaded 506 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored. No separate refutation pass: the cold review was the adversarial pass on this exact prototype (15-pin red-first audit, theorem attacks, live A4 reproduction) and the build applied it verbatim plus one prose guidepost; the coordinator independently verified the committed tree, the doctest surface and the gates.

comments.text: RESEARCH DONE (2026-09-03, prototype proto184.diff in the coordinator's scratchpad, being cold-reviewed). THE RULE: each @spec variable gets LOWER bounds from covariant occurrences (joined) and UPPER bounds from contravariant ones (met, under an arrow's parameters -- the ONE reversing node, collect_arrow_match); instantiation is the join of the lower bounds and nothing else; the meet is the solvability CHECK (lower ⊄ upper → Invalid); a variable with only upper bounds stays free. Verdicts base → rule: A4 Known (any)->nil (unsound) → Known (int)->nil; A5 Invalid (false violation) → Known int; A3 a := any → int; A13 filter result [any] → [int]; A2 Known [any] → Underconstrained; all other attacks unchanged; 14 attacks promoted to named tests + a meet-check witness (arrow_match 35/0). Code: BindingSide { Unify, Lower, Upper } in types/mod.rs (collect_instantiation_subst documented as the UNIFIER, four callers byte-identical; new collect_constraint_subst is the solver), MatchBounds { lower, upper } through the six collectors, merge_subst_meet, upper bounds read from the RAW ARGUMENTS (the witnesses erase them: fz-kdt.192). CORPUS (597, base 0889c0b3a): 0 behaviour movers on interp and run, 0 canon movers, executables/any-returns/FIFO-LIFO set identical -- yet the path is exercised 52,475 times, 24,556 upper bindings base unioned are discarded and 912 Invalids ruled, none reaching a published fact; the defect is latent on the corpus exactly as this ticket predicted. Lib 1627/0/5, matrix 485/0/9. STACKED with fz-kdt.120: a FOLD, not a merge -- 120's OpenVars.positive/flipped() IS BindingSide and 120's open_vars walk is 184's args walk; the stacked tree is byte-identical to pure 120 on the corpus; four arrow_match pins flip to 120's deliberate decisions (A7/A8/A9 → Underconstrained, A3's b half → [] | [int]). Hand-off: 120 re-cut on top of 184. Note: the false doc sentence this ticket names ("only the arrow's RESULT feeds the union") is not at HEAD; it arrives with 120's diff, which is the sequencing rationale.

UPDATE from the fz-kdt.192 cold review (2026-09-03): (1) STRIKE fix 2 ('never record an upper bound of none') -- ablation on 184-on-192 is inert (corpus 0/0/0, identical 13 pins); R20 stays Underconstrained under 192 so its witness is gone. (2) R2 (union-of-arrows → Invalid) is already delivered by 192 without polarity machinery, so it is not this ticket's red-first witness; the polarity split's red-first witnesses are A4 (unsound (any)->nil → (int)->nil) and A5 (false Invalid → Known int), A13/A3 the precision wins; the solvability gate itself is justified by the theorem and its ablation on the reduce-at-(binary,int)->int shape, not by a HEAD-red corpus witness -- say so in the doc. (3) Re-cut on 192: +247/−47 (arrow_match +178/−37, types/mod.rs +69/−10), 13 pin literals, R5/R20 hold, corpus 0/0/0. (4) fix 3 becomes the one-line has_vars guard on the position.

Sequence update (2026-09-03): fz-kdt.183 LANDED (2e0bb2706, independent of this ticket; it does not touch arrow_match.rs), fz-kdt.124 CLOSED as refuted. Live order is now 198 -> 192 -> 184 -> 120. 192 is built and refuted (bcca85148 on wt/kdt192-build, waiting only on 198), so this ticket re-cuts on THAT commit: the builder must re-measure R20 there before deciding whether "never record an upper bound of none" is still needed (192 folded D1 and made the witness the raw argument, which changes where a `[]` under an arrow parameter is read from). R2 stays the red-first witness.

fz-kdt.192 landed (343f3a134): base for this ticket's re-cut. The re-cut must DELETE: the `args` parameter on instantiate_match and the second full walk per position (192 has one walk over (params, args)); the discarded position.upper / observed.lower from that walk and the dropped MatchWitness with no `let _`; every match_witness / overlapping_witnesses edit; the "upper bounds from the raw ARGUMENTS" doc paragraph. Fix 2 ("never record an upper bound of none") is STRUCK -- its witness R20 is Underconstrained here. Fix 3 collapses to a one-line `if !has_vars(witness)` guard on the position. "Promote R2 as the gate's red-first witness" is SUBSUMED: R2 is already Invalid at 192 (reached with no polarity machinery), so the polarity split's red-first witnesses are A4 (unsound (any)->nil → (int)->nil) and A5 (false Invalid → Known int); the solvability gate ships on the theorem and its ablation. The pin literals this ticket updates live in pinned_verdicts (52 pins in arrow_match.rs + 4 in contract_test.rs).

title: A @spec variable collects lower bounds from covariant occurrences and upper bounds from contravariant ones: instantiation is the join of the lowers, the meet of the uppers is the solvability check
